summary: Backend-only verification of the refresh-token GRACE window fix in routes/auth.py that prevents mobile forced-logout on concurrent refresh with the same refresh token. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_refresh_grace_iter33.py with 9 tests: login+/me (employee & admin), 3-step rotation chain, sequential double-use within grace (both 200), 8-way concurrent burst via httpx.AsyncClient+asyncio.gather (all 200 + a successor still refreshes), logout revocation regression, invalid/missing refresh token 401s, and time-off create+admin-list regression. ALL 9 PASSED. The core bug fix is confirmed: reusing the same R1 concurrently now returns 200 for every caller instead of the prior 401 'Refresh token revoked'.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py refresh() correctly uses an atomic find_one_and_update CAS on {jti, revoked_at: None} — only one caller mints the successor; losers fall through to grace-window handling. Good.

Grace window (60s) issues a NEW family-preserving token pair to grace-path callers. Note: this multiplies successor tokens per burst (e.g. 8 concurrent -> 1 winner + 7 grace tokens, all valid). This is acceptable for the mobile use case but is worth being aware of — the family, not the token count, is the theft-boundary.
Reuse-outside-grace path revokes the entire family via update_many — correct and matches the doc comment.

Minor: refresh() function shadows the imported 'payload' variable name with the decoded token dict (parameter `payload: dict | None` then reassigned from decode_token). Works but is confusing; consider renaming.
Index on refresh_tokens(family_id, revoked_at) supports the family-revoke path; verify a jti index also exists for the CAS hot path (likely already there via prior iterations).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 33 confirmed the refresh grace-window fix end-to-end against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Full test lives at /app/backend/tests/test_refresh_grace_iter33.py — reuse it as a regression. The 60s-expiry theft-revoke path (reuse AFTER grace) was NOT tested (would require sleep>60s); if a future agent wants to verify it, wait ~65s then re-present an already-rotated token and expect 401 plus revoked_at set on all family tokens. Run with: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> python -m pytest tests/test_refresh_grace_iter33.py -v -o addopts=''.
rca of the issue: Prior bug: refresh() eagerly revoked the presented refresh token before minting the successor. Mobile RN runs multiple JS runtimes (foreground + background tasks + push handlers) that share one stored refresh token; when the 15-min (now 30-min) access token expired they'd all POST /auth/refresh in parallel. First request rotated the token; siblings then saw revoked_at set and got 401 'Refresh token revoked', which the app treated as a signed-out state -> forced login screen especially after connectivity blips. Fix: (a) atomic find_one_and_update CAS designates one winner per jti; (b) losers within 60s grace get a fresh valid pair in the SAME token family instead of 401; (c) reuse beyond grace revokes the whole family, preserving theft detection; (d) ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES raised 15->30 to reduce refresh frequency. Verified by concurrent 8x burst — all 200.
